title: A Therapist's View of the Good Life: The Fully Functioning Person
coreMove: Choose fuller contact with reality over a protected version of happiness.
sourcePressure: The good life is described as fuller functioning, openness, and flexible process rather than stable comfort or permanent composure. Frozen sidecar ch09 supports the heading, part placement, and broad thematic claims; it exposes no chapter-local named anecdotes, studies, or places.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Equating the good life with ease, serenity, or inspirational flourishing.
sourceAnchorNote: The frozen source exposes no usable chapter-local named person, study, institution, place, date, or anecdotal artifact from Rogers here. Use fictional protagonists only; do not invent named Rogers cases or studies.

hook: opening with a definition of good life
counterintuition: Most people think X, but Y
It is not about being nice
The paradox is that acceptance changes everything
